summary: Updates RFC 5480 to specify what the keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment key usage bits mean in certificates that support elliptic curve cryptography.

eli5.summary: A clarification of what two permission labels on a digital ID mean for a certain type of key.

questions: what does keyencipherment mean for ecc certificates
what does rfc 8813 change in rfc 5480
subtitle: Elliptic curve certificates must not set the keyEncipherment or dataEncipherment key usage bits.

tldr.problem: RFC 5480 specified 7 of the 9 key usage values for elliptic curve keys but did not mention keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8813 adds text to Section 3 of RFC 5480: if keyUsage is present, those two values MUST NOT be present for id-ecPublicKey, id-ecDH or id-ecMQV keys.
tldr.outcome: The omission is closed, so ECC certificates are clear about which usage bits are forbidden.

today: RFC 8813 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5480. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: The Omission in RFC 5480
sections.content:
RFC 5480 defines the Subject Public Key Information field for certificates that support Elliptic Curve Cryptography. It also says which combinations of values are permitted for the key usage extension from RFC 5280.

It specifies 7 of the 9 values and says nothing about keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment. RFC 8813 corrects this by adding text to the end of Section 3 of RFC 5480.
sections.eli5: A rulebook explained seven of nine permission labels. This note covers the other two.

sections.title: The New Requirements
sections.content:
If the keyUsage extension is present in a certificate that indicates id-ecPublicKey in SubjectPublicKeyInfo, then keyEncipherment and dataEncipherment MUST NOT be present.

The same holds for certificates that indicate id-ecDH or id-ecMQV: those two values also MUST NOT be present.
sections.eli5: A certain kind of digital ID is never allowed to carry two particular permission stickers.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The document introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 5480, and it has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: This clarification adds no new danger and needs no list updates.
